newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, Hong Kong set further shipping talks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, Hong Kong set further shipping talks.

text.p: Taiwan and Hong Kong plan a second round of talks aiming to overcome sovereignty hurdles that threaten to halt bilateral shipping after the British colony reverts to China in July, officials said on Wednesday.
"The talks should resume next week, most likely on Monday and Tuesday, in Taipei," a transport ministry spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.
"Flag-flying remains the key issue in the talks," she said.

Talks on direct shipping after Hong Kong's July 1 handover ended without agreement on May 2 after the sides failed to agree on which flags ships should fly when plying routes between Hong Kong and Taiwan.
Beijing's Communist government objects to any ship entering Hong Kong harbour flying Taiwan's Nationalist Republic of China flag.
The Nationalists lost a civil war to the Communists on the mainland and fled to island in 1949.
Taipei has said it would welcome ships flying Communist China's red five-star -- but only if those flying Taiwan's republican flag are welcome in Hong Kong.
Transport vice-minister Hsu Chieh-kuei, quoted by the ministry spokeswoman, said Taiwan viewed reciprocity and equality as preconditions for future direct shipping between Hong Kong and Taiwan.
Taiwan's negotiator in the May 2 talks, Chang Liang-jen of the quasi-official Straits Exchange Foundation, has singled out the flag issue as the main obstacle to agreement.
"It's a very complicated matter and a difficult one to settle just in one meeting," he said after the first round.
Ships registered in Hong Kong and Taiwan currently follow the international practice of flying each other's flag when entering the other's territorial waters.
This practice would end after Britain hands Hong Kong back to China, as the territory's post-handover constitution has a clause saying it must observe the "one-China" principle.

Such a breakdown would be extremely costly for Hong Kong, Taiwan and China, and several options are under consideration to avoid it, including flying no flags at all or reregistering all ships under third-country flags.

Communist China has viewed Taiwan as a rebel-held province since the civil war that sent the Nationalists into exile and maintains that the island must eventually be brought under Beijing's sovereignty.
